posts.subject: The sea gave the road back
posts.instagramCaption:
The sea gave the road back.

After one violent night, two fishers found a Vanir causeway where the tide should have been. They reached the arch just as the sea returned—and something beneath it woke.

Watch to the end: would you enter?

This is an original Nordic fantasy world being created by Thomas Robbjens. Follow the continuing story of The Land of Roo.

Concept art from The Land of Roo.

posts.facebookCaption:
The sea gave an ancient road back.

After a violent night storm, two Rooan fishers found an immense Vanir causeway exposed beneath the tide. They crossed it before the water returned. At the final arch, a line of light appeared beneath the sea.

Watch to the end. Would you enter—or turn back while you still could?

The Land of Roo is an original Nordic fantasy world being created by Thomas Robbjens. Follow the continuing story.

posts.subject: The river allows one crossing
posts.instagramCaption:
The river will allow one crossing.

Swipe: the spring flood has taken the bridge. The healer carries medicine for a fevered village. The farmer carries the only seed grain for spring. The ferry can take one before the next surge.

Medicine—or seed? Comment one word.

posts.subject: The door had no hinges
posts.instagramCaption:
The door had no hinges.

Secrets of the Vanir

A storm uprooted an ancient spruce and exposed this beneath its roots. No handle. No lock. Only a warm line of light around stone that should have been dead.

Mark the path—or run?

Follow for the next Roo mystery.

posts.facebookCaption:
The storm uncovered a door with no hinges.

Secrets of the Vanir

A Rooan woodcutter found it beneath the roots of an ancient spruce. The stone has no handle and no lock, yet a warm line of light runs around its edge. He has told no one where it is.

Would you mark the path and return with others—or leave before it opens?

Follow for the next Roo mystery.
